text:
Fixed. The issue was that the regex `[^a-z0-9]` replaced each non-alphanumeric character individually with a hyphen, producing runs of hyphens and leading/trailing hyphens. I changed it to `[^a-z0-9]+` (collapse consecutive non-alphanumerics into a single hyphen) and added `.strip("-")` to remove leading/trailing hyphens.

Verification:
- `slugify("Hello,  World!")` → `"hello-world"` ✓
- `slugify("--a--b--")` → `"a-b"` ✓
- `slugify("Hello World")` → `"hello-world"` ✓
- All tests pass; public signature unchanged.

arguments.summary: Fixed slugify in textkit/slug.py by changing the replacement regex from `[^a-z0-9]` to `[^a-z0-9]+` so consecutive non-alphanumeric characters collapse into a single hyphen, and added `.strip("-")` to remove leading/trailing hyphens. This makes `slugify("Hello,  World!")` return `"hello-world"` and ...
